semantics.note: Faithfully keeps 'to my mind' and 'many'. It is an evaluative aggregate judgment about unnamed arguments, not a bounded factual claim.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no stable support or contradiction condition: the arguments aren't listed, 'many' has no threshold and 'misrepresentation' is undefined.

reviews.rationale: This is an opinion about an unspecified set of opponents' arguments, with no count and no definition of misrepresentation. Picking particular arguments would create a new proposition. The packet has no evidence items. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Keeps 'most or all', the lobbying group, the forceful opposition and the broad public support. 'Fought hard' fairly paraphrases 'tooth and nail'.

contract.note: The plain reading (five big tech firms, a majority affiliated, sustained public opposition, majority support in polls) is ordinary and fair, and it weighs contrary polls.

evidence.note: Contemporary report (Aug 7, 2024): Chamber of Progress is backed by Amazon, Apple, Google and Meta, 4 of the 5 firms.
The organization's own June 2024 lobbying letter states continued opposition and urges legislators to oppose SB 1047. Primary record of its lobbying.
AIPI poll of California voters, public by July 23: 59% support, 20% oppose. The pollster advocates regulation, but the majority is clear.
CalChamber poll fielded Aug 9–12: 46% oppose. Its question was heavily slanted (fines, firms leaving), so it is not comparable and doesn't defeat broad support.

reviews.rationale: A majority of the big tech group (4 of 5) backs Chamber of Progress, which formally and repeatedly urged opposition to SB 1047. The July poll showed clear majority support. The contrary August poll was slanted, so it is context. Supported on the plain reading.
